properties.description:
At 1201 PM EDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a tornado
was located over Fayetteville, moving northeast at 35 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed. Damage
to roofs, windows, and vehicles will occur.  Tree damage is
likely.

This dangerous storm will be near...
Fayetteville around 1205 PM EDT.

Other locations impacted by this tornadic thunderstorm include Bonnie
Doone.
properties.instruction:
TAKE COVER NOW! Move to a basement or an interior room on the lowest
floor of a sturdy building. Avoid windows. If you are outdoors, in a
mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter
and protect yourself from flying debris.

If a tornado or other severe weather is spotted, report it to the
National Weather Service or your local nearest law enforcement agency
who will send your report. This act may save lives of others in the
path of dangerous weather.

The National Weather Service in Wilmington has issued a

Central Columbus County in southeastern North Carolina...

to roofs, windows and vehicles will occur. Tree damage is

properties.headline: Blowing Dust Advisory issued October 11 at 8:57AM PDT until October 11 at 5:00PM PDT by NWS Spokane WA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Patchy to localized areas of blowing dust expected, with
visibility dropping to between one-quarter and one mile at times.
Northeast winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts of 35 mph.

* WHERE...Othello, Harrington, Odessa, Grand Coulee, Quincy, Moses
Lake, Wilbur, Coulee City, Ephrata, Ritzville, and Creston.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM PDT this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Hazardous driving conditions due to reduced visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Light showers moved through the area this
morning with rainfall amounts varying from a trace to few
hundreths.  Northeast winds have increased however the threat for
blowing dust will be delayed until conditions dry out.
properties.instruction:
Be ready for a sudden drop in visibility to one mile or less. If you
encounter blowing dust or blowing sand on the roadway or see it
approaching, pull off the road as far as possible and put your
vehicle in park. Turn the lights all the way off and keep foot off
the brake pedal. Remember, 'Pull Aside, Stay Alive'.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...In Alabama, Mobile Coastal and Baldwin Coastal
Counties. In Florida, Escambia Coastal, Santa Rosa Coastal and
Okaloosa Coastal Counties.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM CDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:

float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.
